quizzes.title: California Commercial Driver (Class A/B) Practice Test #1
quizzes.description: California DMV Class A or B commercial driver's license (CDL) practice test #1. Real questions covering general knowledge, air brakes, combination vehicles and pre-trip inspection.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection of your commercial vehicle should be performed:
options: At least once a week.
Only if any problems occurred the last time the vehicle was operated.
Before operating the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Federal and state regulations require commercial drivers to inspect their vehicle before every trip to identify any safety defects before driving.

questions.question: To stay safe while driving at night, you should:
options: Drive slowly enough to stop within the range of your headlights in emergencies.
Roll down the window for fresh air to stay awake.
Drink coffee or other caffeinated beverages if you become sleepy.
questions.explanation: Your headlights only illuminate so far ahead. Driving at a speed that lets you stop within that distance is essential to avoid hitting unseen obstacles at night.

questions.question: The term used to describe the rear wheels of a commercial vehicle following a different path than the front wheels while turning is:
options: Sidetracking.
Offtracking.
Fishtailing.
questions.explanation: Offtracking occurs when the rear wheels of a long vehicle take a shorter path than the front wheels through a turn, which is why CDL drivers must swing wide.

questions.question: When dealing with a pressurized cooling system, you should:
options: Check the coolant level only when the engine has cooled.
Safely remove the radiator cap and add coolant while the engine is hot.
Use water only in the cooling system.
questions.explanation: Hot pressurized coolant can spray out violently and cause serious burns. Always let the engine cool before opening the cap or checking the level.

questions.question: If you must park on the side of a road at night, you should:
options: Turn on your 4-way emergency flashers.
Place warning devices within 15 minutes.
Use your left turn signal lights.
questions.explanation: Activating the 4-way emergency flashers warns approaching traffic of your stopped vehicle. Reflective triangles must also be placed within 10 minutes.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection of the steering system, which of the following would require immediate repair?
options: Too many vertical stacks.
Oil on the tie rod.
Steering wheel play exceeding 10 degrees.
questions.explanation: More than 10 degrees (about 2 inches on a 20-inch wheel) of steering wheel play makes it difficult to steer accurately and is unsafe.

questions.question: Containerized loads:
options: Are exempt from hazardous materials restrictions.
Are exempt from weight limits.
Are generally used for transporting freight by rail or ship.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are sealed cargo containers designed for intermodal transport (truck, rail, and ship). They must still comply with hazmat and weight regulations.

questions.question: Approaching a downhill curved offramp, you should:
options: Do nothing because the posted limits account for safety.
Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
Downshift after entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Brake to a safe speed before entering the curve. Posted speeds on offramps are designed for cars; trucks must drive slower because of their higher center of gravity.

questions.question: Which method of fire suppression is safe?
options: Water on electrical fires.
Water on gasoline fires.
Neither of the above.
questions.explanation: Water conducts electricity (worsening electrical fires) and spreads gasoline fires. Use a B:C or A:B:C rated fire extinguisher instead.

questions.question: Total stopping distance is the sum of:
options: Perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance.
Observation distance, reaction distance, and slowing distance.
Perception distance, response distance, and reaction distance.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance is perception distance (seeing the hazard) + reaction distance (moving foot to brake) + braking distance (vehicle slowing to a stop).

questions.question: When checking your trailer connection, you should make sure that:
options: The fifth wheel is tilted upward.
There is no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
The kingpin is bent.
questions.explanation: Any gap between the upper and lower fifth wheel means the connection isn't secure and the trailer could come loose.

questions.question: When driving with air brakes, what is brake lag?
options: The time it takes for brakes to wear out.
The time it takes for air to flow through the lines when the brake pedal is pressed.
The time it takes to move your foot from the accelerator to the brake.
questions.explanation: Air brakes have a built-in lag (about a half second) because compressed air must travel through the brake lines before brakes engage. This adds to total stopping distance.

questions.question: What should you do if you experience brake failure while going down a grade?
options: Pull onto the shoulder and wait for help.
Use an escape ramp if one is available.
Shift to neutral to reduce wear on the brakes.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are designed to stop runaway vehicles safely. Always use one if available rather than continuing down the grade.

questions.question: What documents must you have in your possession while operating with a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
options: Just your CLP.
Your CLP and a valid driver's license.
Your CLP, a valid driver's license, and a medical examiner's certificate.
questions.explanation: CLP holders must carry the CLP, their underlying valid driver's license, and a current medical examiner's certificate while operating a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: What is counter steering?
options: Turning the steering wheel counter clockwise.
Steering in the opposite direction from what other drivers expect.
Turning the wheel in the opposite direction after steering to avoid a traffic emergency.
questions.explanation: Counter steering is the corrective step taken after an emergency swerve, when you bring the wheel back to straighten the vehicle after avoiding a hazard.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you must stop within how many feet of the nearest rail if you transport passengers or hazardous materials?
options: 5 to 25 feet.
15 to 50 feet.
100 feet or more.
questions.explanation: Passenger buses, school buses, and hazmat vehicles must stop between 15 and 50 feet of the nearest rail at all railroad crossings.

questions.question: When backing a commercial vehicle, you should:
options: Back toward the driver's side whenever possible.
Back toward the passenger's side whenever possible.
Rely on your mirrors only and never get out of the cab.
questions.explanation: Backing toward the driver's side gives you a much better view of where you're going. Avoid blind-side (passenger-side) backing whenever possible.

questions.question: How can you tell if your vehicle is hydroplaning?
options: The steering will feel heavy and stiff.
The steering will feel light, and the rear of the vehicle may slide.
The brake pedal will pulse rapidly.
questions.explanation: When tires lose contact with the road surface and ride on a film of water, steering becomes very light and the rear may begin to slide. Ease off the accelerator until traction returns.

questions.question: Which of the following items is NOT considered part of the pre-trip inspection?
options: Checking tire pressure.
Checking that all required emergency equipment is on board.
Tuning the radio.
questions.explanation: Pre-trip inspections focus on safety items: tires, brakes, lights, cargo, fluids, and emergency equipment. Adjusting the radio is not safety-related.

questions.question: If you are convicted of driving a commercial vehicle while under the influence of alcohol (BAC 0.04% or higher), you will lose your CDL for at least:
options: 30 days.
6 months.
1 year.
questions.explanation: A first DUI offense while operating a CMV results in a minimum one-year CDL disqualification. A second offense results in a lifetime disqualification.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth required on the front (steering) tires of a commercial vehicle?
options: 2/32 inch.
4/32 inch.
6/32 inch.
questions.explanation: Steer-axle tires must have at least 4/32 inch tread depth in every major groove. Other tires require at least 2/32 inch.

questions.question: What is the proper way to test hydraulic brakes for leaks?
options: Pump the pedal three times, apply firm pressure, hold for five seconds, and see if the pedal moves.
Push down on the pedal once and listen for hissing.
Drive slowly and brake hard.
questions.explanation: If the pedal moves under steady pressure, you may have a leak in the hydraulic brake system. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: When loading cargo, the weight should be:
options: Concentrated as high as possible.
Distributed as low as possible and balanced.
Placed entirely toward the rear.
questions.explanation: A low, balanced load lowers the center of gravity and reduces the risk of rollover. Improperly loaded high cargo increases tip-over risk during turns.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about communicating with other drivers?
options: You should signal your intentions and tap the brake lightly to flash brake lights when slowing.
Only use the horn in heavy traffic.
Flash your high beams continuously to warn drivers behind.
questions.explanation: Signaling, tapping the brakes to flash the lights, and using the horn appropriately are all part of communicating with other drivers safely.

questions.question: If your truck has dual tires, you should check that:
options: The tires are touching each other.
There is space between the tires and they are not touching.
Both tires have different tread patterns.
questions.explanation: Dual tires must not touch each other or rub on other parts of the vehicle. Touching tires generate heat and can cause blowouts.

questions.question: What is the safest way to handle a tire blowout on a front tire?
options: Brake hard and steer toward the shoulder.
Stay off the brake, hold the steering wheel firmly, and let the vehicle slow before pulling off the road.
Accelerate to maintain control.
questions.explanation: Heavy braking after a blowout can cause loss of control. Grip the wheel firmly, let the vehicle slow naturally, then gently steer off the road.

questions.question: The proper way to test the parking brake is to:
options: Drive at high speed and pull it on.
Stop the vehicle, put it in low gear, release the service brake, set the parking brake, and gently apply power.
Push down the brake pedal and hold it for 1 minute.
questions.explanation: With the parking brake set, gently apply power in low gear. The vehicle should remain still. This confirms the parking brake will hold the vehicle.

questions.question: What does ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) do for a commercial vehicle?
options: It shortens your stopping distance significantly.
It helps you maintain steering control during hard braking by preventing wheel lockup.
It eliminates the need for normal braking technique.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheels from locking up under hard braking so you can steer to avoid hazards. It does not necessarily shorten stopping distance.

questions.question: When inspecting your vehicle, you find that the air leakage rate is higher than the maximum allowed. You should:
options: Continue your trip and have it checked at the destination.
Have the system repaired before driving.
Drive only at low speeds.
questions.explanation: Excessive air leakage means the brakes cannot be relied on. The system must be repaired before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: At what point should you use the trailer hand valve in normal driving?
options: To park the vehicle.
To test the trailer brakes only; never as a regular service brake.
Every time you slow down.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve should only be used to test the trailer brakes. Using it for normal braking can cause the trailer to skid or jackknife.

quizzes.title: California Commercial Driver (Class A/B) Practice Test #2
quizzes.description: California DMV Class A or B commercial driver's license (CDL) practice test #2. Real questions covering general knowledge, air brakes, combination vehicles and pre-trip inspection.

questions.question: You are about to go down a long, steep, downhill grade in a newer truck. You should:
options: Use a lower gear than you would use to climb the uphill grade.
Use the same gear you would use to climb the uphill grade.
Use a higher gear than you would use to climb the uphill grade.
questions.explanation: Newer trucks with more aerodynamic designs and improved drivetrains require a lower gear going down a steep grade than they would going up the same grade.

questions.question: Which of these items is checked during a pre-trip inspection?
options: Cargo securement.
Whether all vehicle lights are working and are clean.
Both cargo securement and vehicle lights.
questions.explanation: A complete pre-trip inspection covers cargo securement, all vehicle lights, brakes, tires, fluid levels, and many other safety items.

questions.question: If you are stopped on a one-way or divided highway, you should place reflective triangles at:
options: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward approaching traffic.
25 feet, 100 feet, and 250 feet toward approaching traffic.
50 feet, 100 feet, and 300 feet toward approaching traffic.
questions.explanation: On a one-way or divided highway, place reflective triangles at 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward approaching traffic.

questions.question: When heavy fog occurs, you should:
options: Use high beams for best visibility.
Park off to the right side of the road with parking lights on.
Park at a rest area or truck stop until the fog has lifted.
questions.explanation: The safest option in heavy fog is to wait it out at a safe location. If you must drive, use low beams (high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility).

questions.question: You should plan ahead when you park your vehicle so that:
options: It will be very easy for you to check your vehicle before you get back on the road.
You are only required to pull forward when you leave.
You don't need to back up more than ten feet.
questions.explanation: Parking strategically lets you easily inspect the vehicle before continuing and helps you leave without dangerous blind-side backing maneuvers.

questions.question: The term 'Gross Combination Weight' refers to:
options: Total weight of a powered unit and the trailer.
Total weight of the trailer and the load.
Total weight of a powered unit, the trailer, and the cargo.
questions.explanation: Gross Combination Weight (GCW) is the total weight of the powered unit (tractor), the trailer, and the cargo being carried.

questions.question: A driver should look how far ahead of the vehicle while driving?
options: 2 to 5 seconds.
12 to 15 seconds.
20 to 30 seconds.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers should look 12 to 15 seconds ahead (about a quarter mile at highway speed) to anticipate hazards early.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about overhead clearance?
options: Posted signs for overhead clearance are always correct.
Paving a road does not affect the clearance height under bridges.
Cargo weight may change the height of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: A heavily loaded truck rides lower than an empty one. Cargo weight (and changes to roadway pavement) can affect actual clearance, so posted heights are not always reliable.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true when performing a pre-trip inspection on brakes and suspension?
options: Brake shoes should be free of oil, grease, and brake fluid.
One missing leaf spring is not dangerous.
A cracked spring hanger is not dangerous.
questions.explanation: Contaminants on the brake shoes greatly reduce braking effectiveness. Any missing leaf spring or cracked spring hanger is dangerous and must be repaired.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because:
options: Exhaust noise will damage the driver's ears.
Toxic fumes and gases could enter the cab or sleeper berth.
The leaking exhaust smoke pollutes the air.
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide and other toxic fumes into the cab, which can sicken or kill the driver.

questions.question: Whenever you stop for a break during your trip, you should:
options: Call in and check with dispatch.
Check critical items such as the tires, brakes, and cargo tie-downs.
Check critical items such as the windshield wipers, heater, and defroster.
questions.explanation: En-route inspections (during breaks) require checking critical safety items: tires, brakes, and cargo securement, in particular.

questions.question: What is the most important hand signal that you and your helper should agree on when backing?
options: A signal meaning 'slow down.'
A signal meaning 'stop.'
A signal meaning 'turn left.'
questions.explanation: Stop is the most critical signal because it is needed to prevent collisions during backing. Driver and helper must agree on it clearly before starting.

questions.question: What two things should you do if a fire happens in your tire on the road?
options: Park the vehicle as soon as possible and use a fire extinguisher to put out the fire.
Drive to the nearest fire station.
Pour water from a water bottle on the tire.
questions.explanation: Stop right away in a safe location and use a fire extinguisher. Continuing to drive will fan the flames and could damage the vehicle further.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, you should:
options: Stay as close to the fire as possible.
Stay upwind so the fire blows away from you, and aim at the base of the fire.
Aim at the top of the flames.
questions.explanation: Stand upwind 6 to 8 feet from the fire, aim the extinguisher at the base of the flames, and sweep side to side until the fire is out.

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of fatigued driving?
options: Drifting from your lane and missing exits.
Singing along with the radio.
Drinking water frequently.
questions.explanation: Drifting out of your lane, missing exits, frequent yawning, and trouble keeping your eyes open are all warning signs of fatigue. Pull over and rest.

questions.question: If your vehicle hydroplanes, you should:
options: Brake hard immediately.
Release the accelerator and push in the clutch to let the wheels slow down.
Accelerate to power through the water.
questions.explanation: Hard braking can cause skidding. Releasing the accelerator (and clutching) lets the tires regain contact with the road surface.

questions.question: On wet roads, you should reduce your speed by:
options: About one-third (e.g., from 55 to 35 mph).
About one-quarter.
About one-half.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed by about one-third on wet roads. On snow, reduce speed by one-half. On ice, reduce speed to a crawl and stop as soon as it is safe.

questions.question: Which axle of a commercial vehicle is most likely to skid because it has less weight?
options: The drive axle.
The trailer axle on an empty trailer.
The steering axle.
questions.explanation: A lightly loaded or empty trailer has less weight pressing the tires down, which means less traction and a higher chance of skidding.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of serious vehicle skids?
options: Worn-out brake pads.
Driving too fast for road conditions.
Worn tires.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast for road conditions is the leading cause of skids. Speed should always be adjusted for weather, traffic, and road surface.

questions.question: If a drive-wheel skid occurs (the rear wheels slide sideways), you should:
options: Stop braking, push in the clutch, and steer in the direction you want to go.
Brake hard and hold the wheel straight.
Speed up to straighten the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stop braking to let the wheels turn freely, push the clutch in to disconnect the drive train, and counter-steer toward where you want the vehicle to go.

questions.question: What is the proper way to hold the steering wheel?
options: With one hand at the bottom.
With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands inside the wheel for better grip.
questions.explanation: Keep both hands firmly on opposite sides of the wheel (about 9 and 3 o'clock). Hands inside the wheel can cause severe injury if the wheel jerks.

questions.question: When making a right turn at an intersection in a large vehicle, you should:
options: Swing wide to the left before turning.
Turn wide as you complete the turn (keep the rear of the vehicle close to the curb).
Use the left lane to make the turn.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb while turning to prevent other drivers from passing on the right and being trapped between you and the curb.

questions.question: How can you avoid jackknifing a trailer?
options: Brake hard with the trailer hand valve.
Avoid hard braking, especially while turning, and use the service brake gently.
Always speed up through curves.
questions.explanation: Jackknifing happens when the trailer pushes the tractor sideways, often from braking too hard. Brake gently, especially in curves, and never rely on the hand valve.

questions.question: When uncoupling a trailer, what should you do before pulling the tractor away?
options: Lower the landing gear until it firmly supports the trailer.
Drive forward a few feet to test the connection.
Apply the trailer parking brake only.
questions.explanation: The landing gear must be fully supporting the trailer's weight before the kingpin is released, or the trailer can fall when the tractor pulls away.

questions.question: When inspecting the air brake system, the warning device for low air pressure should activate before pressure drops below:
options: 20 psi.
60 psi.
100 psi.
questions.explanation: The low-air warning must activate before pressure falls below 60 psi. Below that level, brakes lose stopping power and emergency brakes may apply.

questions.question: What does it mean if the spring brakes apply automatically while you are driving?
options: The system is functioning normally.
There is a major air loss, and you should stop and have the system checked.
You should release the parking brake and continue driving.
questions.explanation: Spring (emergency) brakes apply automatically when air pressure drops too low. This indicates a major leak, and the vehicle must be repaired before continuing.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about cargo securement?
options: Cargo should be inspected once at the start of the trip.
Cargo must be inspected within the first 50 miles and every 150 miles or 3 hours after that.
Only oversize loads require securement inspection during a trip.
questions.explanation: Drivers must re-check cargo within the first 50 miles, then every 150 miles or every 3 hours (whichever comes first), and after every break.

questions.question: What is the best way to check that your headlights are working before a trip?
options: Turn them on and walk around the vehicle to look at them.
Listen for a clicking noise.
Wait until it gets dark.
questions.explanation: Walk around the vehicle to confirm all lights actually illuminate. Doing so finds burned-out bulbs, dirty lenses, and wiring problems.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign your vehicle's brakes are out of adjustment?
options: Stopping power is reduced and stopping distance increases.
The brakes feel firmer than usual.
The engine runs rougher.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes cannot deliver full braking force, which increases stopping distance. Brakes must be inspected and adjusted regularly.

questions.question: Empty trucks require ____ stopping distances than fully loaded trucks because empty trucks have ____ traction.
options: Shorter; more.
Longer; less.
The same; equal.
questions.explanation: An empty truck has less weight pressing the tires onto the road, which reduces traction and means brakes can lock up sooner, lengthening stopping distance.
